summary: A short, non-interactive status label like Draft, Published or Failed. The words carry the meaning; the tone reinforces it.
whenToUse: Showing the status of one item in a list, a table row or a card header.
Match the tone to the meaning: success for done or healthy, warning for needs attention, danger for failed or blocked, info for new or beta, neutral when there is no judgement.
Keep it to one or two words in sentence case.
whenNotToUse: Anything the user clicks or removes: a badge is plain text, not focusable. Use a small ghost button or a filter chip.
Unread counts on icons: use a counter (not in the system yet).
A sentence or an explanation: use an inline message near the content instead.

dos.title: The text says the status, the tone backs it up
dos.text: Someone who cannot tell green from red still reads "Published" and "Failed".

dos.title: Neutral by default
dos.text: Reserve colored tones for states the user should act on or notice.

donts.title: Color as the only signal
donts.text: Dots without words fail WCAG 1.4.1 and mean nothing to a screen reader.

donts.title: A tone that contradicts the words
donts.text: Danger for "New" borrows urgency the user did not ask for and trains people to ignore red.

accessibility: A badge is static text read in the normal reading order. It needs no role.
Solid tones use color.text.on-solid on feedback.*.solid. Every pair is checked in the contrast matrix, in both themes.
If a status changes while the user is on the page (Running to Failed), announce it with a live region next to the badge; the badge itself is silent.
Never rely on tone alone (WCAG 1.4.1): the text must make sense in grayscale.
